title: Machine-learning microbiome score is associated with future Crohn's disease in relatives
summary: In a prospective cohort of 3483 healthy first-degree relatives of patients with Crohn's disease, machine learning on 16S rRNA gut microbiome composition defined a microbiome risk score (MRS). In an independent validation cohort the MRS gave a hazard ratio of 2.24 (95% CI 1.03-4.84, P = .04) and captured individuals who developed disease up to 5 years before onset (AUC > 0.65). The five most important taxa were Ruminococcus torques, Blautia, Colidextribacter, an uncultured Oscillospiraceae group and Roseburia. The effect is modest and the confidence interval wide; it shows association, not causation.
ai_technology: Machine-learning model on 16S rRNA microbiome composition producing a risk score
organization: Mount Sinai Hospital; University of Toronto

evidence.tested: Score derived in a discovery cohort and tested in an independent validation cohort of the prospective study.
evidence.unknown: Causal role of the taxa and clinical usefulness; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning defined the microbial signature underlying the risk score.
